Frequently asked questions

How much GOSI is deducted from a Saudi employee's salary?

Under the previous system, 9% for the pension branch plus 0.75% for SANED (unemployment insurance), 9.75% in total, on basic salary plus housing allowance up to SAR 45,000 a month. The employer pays 9% pension, 0.75% SANED and 2% occupational hazards, 11.75% in total.

Why do two Saudi employees pay different pension rates?

The new Social Insurance Law of July 2024 applies a graded rate to people who subscribe for the first time from 3 July 2024: it started at 9% and rises by half a point each July until it reaches 11%. Earlier subscribers stay at 9%.

Do non-Saudi employees pay GOSI?

Nothing is deducted from a non-Saudi employee's salary. The employer pays 2% for occupational hazards on the employee's basic salary plus housing.

What salary is GOSI calculated on?

The contributory wage: basic salary plus cash housing allowance, capped at SAR 45,000 a month. Transport and other allowances are not included.

When are contributions paid?

The employer pays each month's contributions, including the employee's deducted share, within the first 15 days of the following month, or a late-payment fine applies.

Sources

  • General Organization for Social Insurance (GOSI)
  • Umm Al-Qura — the new Social Insurance Law (Royal Decree M/273), Arabic
  • Al Eqtisadiah — the graded increase for new subscribers (30 June 2025), Arabic
